narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: the actual specimen the chapter opens on - a single zircon grain whose glowing inner core and paler outer rim hint that one crystal holds two ages, the moon's birth and a later catastrophe.
subject: A single tiny translucent crystal grain, smaller than a grain of salt, gripped at the very tip of a pair of fine metal tweezers. The crystal is lit from within: a small bright glowing core of cyan-teal light at its center, wrapped in a slightly paler, cooler outer rim, with faint concentric growth zones between them. A few other dark mineral specks lie out of focus far below in a shallow pan.
scene: A field-tent laboratory at night, the grain raised to a cold lamp; everything beyond the crystal and the tweezer-tip falls into soft dark, dust motes drifting in the lamp beam.
camera: Extreme macro, the grain and tweezer-tip sharp and large in frame, the background thrown far out of focus into haze.
light: Cool clinical lamp glow plus a stronger bioluminescent-style glow from inside the crystal; deep indigo shadow behind; a faint warm pinpoint deep in the core.
palette: Void-indigo background, cyan and teal glow from the crystal, cool steel grey on the tweezers, one scarce amber spark in the core.
style: Painterly naturalist specimen plate, hand-painted texture, shallow-focus intimacy.
detail_level: Crisp on the crystal's core, rim, and growth zones and the tweezer-tip; everything else dissolving into soft dark haze.
composition: The tweezers entering from one lower corner, the glowing grain at the optical center on a third line, vast dark negative space around it for focus.
consistency_notes: Same glowing layered crystal motif as the cover (bright core, paler rim). Cool Pandora palette, bioluminescent key glow from within the specimen.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon or anime style
